key_insight: An AI model’s public name can stay the same even when the model or its surrounding system changes. The paper argues that meaningful versioning is essential for tracking those changes and supporting reproducible research and regulatory oversight.
problem_solved: Unchanged public identifiers can conceal updates to AI models and system integrations, making it difficult to determine which version was evaluated, used in a study, or subject to oversight.
method: Identify the mismatch between AI system updates and unchanged public identifiers.
Explain how this mismatch undermines scientific reproducibility and regulatory oversight.
Advocate for meaningful AI versioning that serves researchers and regulators.
impact: Meaningful versioning would help practitioners document which AI system they used and interpret results across updates. It would also support clearer accountability when system behavior changes.
visual_elements: A timeline showing multiple AI updates beneath one unchanged public model name.
A before-and-after diagram contrasting opaque naming with clearly versioned releases.
A model-and-integration schematic highlighting that changes can occur beyond the model itself.
Linked icons for version identification, reproducible experiments, and regulatory oversight.
paper_authors: Vasilios Mavroudis, Dan Ristea, Lauritz Morlock, Carlos Mougan
